title: DNS Concepts Practice
subject: DNS
description: Everyday DNS incidents using evidence-first triage → diagnosis → fix. Titles and summaries are symptom-based to keep root cause discovery inside the workflow.
reportOverview: This report summarizes ticket outcomes and change notes for DNS concepts practice. Use it to review your evidence interpretation and troubleshooting path.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Read the symptom and review the evidence.
2) Choose the first thing you would verify (Triage).
3) Pick the most likely cause based on the evidence (Diagnosis).
4) Select the best remediation step (Fix).
5) Write a short change note describing what changed and how you validated it.

tickets.title: New workstation cannot complete domain join
tickets.summary: A newly imaged workstation fails to join the domain. Internet access works, but the domain join wizard reports it cannot locate a domain controller.
validations: Confirm client is using internal DNS (DCs).
Confirm SRV lookup resolves after change.
Retry domain join.

debrief.summary: You reinforced that AD depends on DNS SRV records. A domain join failing with SRV NXDOMAIN strongly points to client DNS misconfiguration (public resolvers instead of internal DC DNS).
debrief.takeaway: You reinforced that AD depends on DNS SRV records.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the affected workstation?
options: Whether the workstation is fully patched and rebooted
Which DNS servers the workstation is using (internal vs public)
Whether NetBIOS over TCP/IP is enabled
Whether the workstation account already exists in AD

diagnosis.q: Based on the evidence, what is the MOST likely reason the join fails?
options: Client is using public DNS and cannot resolve AD SRV records
DC is out of disk space and not responding to LDAP
Time drift between workstation and DC is blocking Kerberos
The DNS zone is configured as Secondary and read-only

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Enable WINS and retry the join
Configure the client (or DHCP option 006) to use DC DNS servers and retry domain join
Disable firewall on the workstation permanently
Create a reverse lookup zone for the workstation subnet

tickets.title: Users cannot reach a server by name but IP works
tickets.summary: Multiple users can reach a server by IP address, but the hostname fails to resolve across clients.
artifact: ping fileserver.contoso.com -> could not find host
*** dc01.contoso.com can't find fileserver.contoso.com: Non-existent domain
validations: Check forward lookup zone record existence.
Validate resolution from multiple clients.
Confirm no conflicting records exist.

debrief.summary: You practiced a classic split: IP connectivity is fine, but name resolution is failing. NXDOMAIN for a known host commonly points to a missing/incorrect host record in the zone (or wrong zone being queried).
debrief.takeaway: You practiced a classic split: IP connectivity is fine, but name resolution is failing.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the DNS server?
options: Whether DNS forwarders are configured
Whether an A record exists for fileserver.contoso.com in the correct zone
Whether scavenging is enabled in the zone
Whether the DHCP scope is issuing correct DNS servers

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause of the failure?
options: The host record is missing or in the wrong zone
Clients are holding a stale cache record
The server is rejecting recursive queries
A conditional forwarder is timing out

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Create/re-register the A record for fileserver.contoso.com (and PTR if required)
Add 8.8.8.8 to client DNS settings permanently
Disable DNS scavenging globally
Create a new root zone named "."

tickets.title: Some clients still reach the old intranet after cutover
tickets.summary: After an intranet migration, most users reach the new server, but a few still connect to an old address or old content.
validations: Verify client cache clears and shows new record.
nslookup returns new IP on affected client.
User reaches new intranet.

debrief.summary: You reinforced the difference between authoritative DNS records and client-side resolver cache. During cutovers, stale cache is a common cause of 'some users only' behavior.
debrief.takeaway: You reinforced the difference between authoritative DNS records and client-side resolver cache.

triage.q: What is the FIRST step on an affected client?
options: Restart the DNS Server service on the DC
Flush the client DNS resolver cache and retest
Delete the intranet record from the DNS zone
Disable IPv6 on the client

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause based on the evidence?
options: Client has a stale cached record that hasn't expired yet
The DNS server is using root hints incorrectly
Zone transfer is failing to the secondary server
The intranet server is blocking ICMP

fix.q: What is the best fix for affected users and future cutovers?
options: Flush DNS cache on affected clients; consider lowering TTL before planned migrations
Disable recursion on DNS servers
Enable non-secure dynamic updates
Create a wildcard A record for contoso.com

tickets.title: Short intranet name does not resolve internally
tickets.summary: Users want to use a short internal name (like http://portal) but it does not resolve inside the network.
artifact: *** dc01.contoso.com can't find portal: Non-existent domain
validations: Confirm portal alias resolves to the correct target.
Confirm clients resolve portal quickly.
Validate portal loads in browser.

debrief.summary: You practiced implementing name convenience without changing the app host: create an alias (CNAME) to point a friendly name at the real host.
debrief.takeaway: You practiced implementing name convenience without changing the app host: create an alias (CNAME) to point a friendly name at the real h…

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST to support a friendly short name like 'portal'?
options: Whether a CNAME (alias) exists for portal in the zone
Whether a reverse lookup zone exists
Whether forwarders are configured
Whether the DNS server is authorized in AD

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely issue?
options: No alias record exists for the short name
Clients have a stale resolver cache
The web server certificate is expired
The DNS server is not responding to UDP 53
Create a CNAME portal -> webserver01.contoso.com and validate resolution
Create PTR records for all clients
Disable secure updates on the zone
Set all clients to use public DNS

tickets.title: Internal names work but external websites do not resolve
tickets.summary: Internal name resolution works, but external names fail across the organization.
validations: Confirm external nslookup succeeds after change.
Confirm internal resolution remains healthy.
Check DNS event logs for timeouts.

debrief.summary: You reinforced the role of upstream resolution. In many enterprise networks, DNS servers must forward to approved resolvers; missing forwarders often causes widespread external resolution failure.
debrief.takeaway: You reinforced the role of upstream resolution.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST on the DNS server for external lookup failures?
options: Forwarders configuration (or approved upstream resolvers)
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether the AD-integrated zone is set to secure updates
Whether the client DNS cache is stale

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause given the evidence?
options: No forwarders are configured and recursion/upstream resolution is failing in this environment
The contoso.com zone is missing a google.com record
The DNS server is not domain-joined
The DHCP scope is exhausted

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Configure valid forwarders (or confirm root hints policy), then retest external resolution
Create a wildcard record for *.com
Disable the DNS Server service and rely on client DNS only
Delete the internal zone and recreate it

tickets.title: Monitoring tool cannot identify devices by IP
tickets.summary: A monitoring/security tool lists many devices only by IP and cannot show hostnames via reverse lookup.
validations: Confirm reverse zone exists for subnet(s).
Confirm PTR lookups return names.
Tool displays hostnames after fix.

debrief.summary: You reinforced that reverse lookups require a properly scoped reverse zone and PTR registration (from DHCP or hosts). Without the zone, PTR queries return NXDOMAIN.
debrief.takeaway: You reinforced that reverse lookups require a properly scoped reverse zone and PTR registration (from DHCP or hosts).

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST to support reverse lookups?
options: That the correct reverse lookup zone exists for the subnet
That forwarders are configured
That scavenging is disabled
That the forward zone is AD-integrated

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause of the PTR lookup failure?
options: Reverse zone is missing (or wrong scope), so PTR queries have nowhere to land
Client cache contains stale PTR records
CNAME records are missing in the forward zone
The DNS server is not authorized in AD
Create the correct reverse lookup zone and ensure PTR registration is enabled/working
Disable recursion on DNS servers
Set all clients to use public DNS
Delete forward lookup zone and rebuild from scratch

tickets.title: External name resolution stopped immediately after a DNS change
tickets.summary: Internal names still resolve, but external names stopped resolving right after a DNS configuration change.
artifact: DNS Manager shows a new zone named "." under Forward Lookup Zones.
validations: Confirm external lookups succeed after fix.
Confirm internal zones continue to resolve.
Check DNS logs for recurrence.

debrief.summary: You identified a high-impact misconfiguration: a root (dot) zone can break recursion. This is a classic 'everything external broke instantly' DNS incident.
debrief.takeaway: You identified a high-impact misconfiguration: a root (dot) zone can break recursion.

triage.q: What is the FIRST thing to check given the evidence?
options: Whether a root zone named "." exists and is intercepting queries
Whether DHCP option 003 is correct
Whether a reverse zone exists
Whether scavenging is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely explanation for external resolution failing immediately?
options: A root zone was created, preventing normal recursion/forwarder usage
All external authoritative servers are down
Client DNS caches are corrupted across the enterprise
The internal AD-integrated zone is read-only

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Delete the "." zone and restart DNS service if needed, then retest
Disable secure dynamic updates
Convert the internal zone to a secondary zone
Change DHCP lease duration

tickets.title: Secondary DNS server shows zone not loaded and missing records
tickets.summary: A secondary DNS server was added for redundancy, but the zone does not populate and shows an error.
artifact: Secondary server: contoso.com shows 'Zone not loaded'
Primary zone transfers: currently not allowing transfers
validations: Confirm zone transfers succeed and records appear.
Validate name resolution from secondary.
Monitor transfer status remains healthy.

debrief.summary: You practiced secondary-zone fundamentals: secondaries rely on zone transfers. If transfers aren’t permitted to the secondary, the zone won’t load/populate.
debrief.takeaway: You practiced secondary-zone fundamentals: secondaries rely on zone transfers.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the primary DNS server?
options: Zone transfer permissions to the secondary server
Forwarders configuration
Reverse zone configuration
DHCP failover configuration

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Zone transfers are blocked or not permitted to the secondary server
Clients are caching negative responses
The secondary server is using public DNS
The internal zone was deleted

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Allow zone transfers to the secondary and verify it can pull the zone
Disable recursion on the primary
Disable secure updates
Create a wildcard record for the zone

tickets.title: DNS changes on one domain controller do not appear on another
tickets.summary: DNS records updated on one domain controller do not show up on the other DC after a long delay.
artifact: Record created on DC1 appears on DC1
Record does not appear on DC2 after 60+ minutes
validations: Confirm replication is healthy after remediation.
Confirm DNS record appears on DC2.
Validate SRV and host records are consistent.

debrief.summary: You reinforced that AD-integrated DNS depends on healthy AD replication. When replication is unhealthy, DNS data consistency breaks across DCs.
debrief.takeaway: You reinforced that AD-integrated DNS depends on healthy AD replication.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST when AD-integrated DNS data is inconsistent between DCs?
options: AD replication health between domain controllers
DNS forwarders configuration
Whether the reverse zone exists
Whether scavenging is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause based on the evidence?
options: AD replication failures are preventing DNS data from replicating
Zone transfers are disabled on AD-integrated zones
Client DNS cache is stale
The zone is configured as Primary on only one DC

fix.q: What is the best fix path?
options: Resolve replication issues (connectivity/DFS-R/Kerberos/time), then confirm DNS data replicates
Delete the DNS zone from DC2 and recreate manually
Disable dynamic updates permanently
Create a root zone named "."

tickets.title: Cannot add DNS records from one server; create option is unavailable
tickets.summary: An administrator cannot add new host records from one DNS server; the 'New Host' option is disabled.
artifact: On DC2 DNS Manager: 'New Host (A or AAAA)' is greyed out
validations: Add record from the writable DNS instance.
Confirm record resolves from clients.
Confirm expected transfer/replication behavior.

debrief.summary: You reinforced writable vs read-only DNS zones. Secondary zones are not editable; records must be added to the primary/writable source (or convert to AD-integrated where appropriate).
debrief.takeaway: You reinforced writable vs read-only DNS zones.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST when record creation is disabled?
options: The zone type (secondary/read-only vs primary/AD-integrated)
DNS forwarders
Reverse lookup zone
DHCP scope utilization

diagnosis.q: Why is record creation unavailable on this server?
options: The server hosts a Secondary zone, which is read-only
The zone is corrupted and must be recreated
The server is not authorized in AD
Clients are using public DNS

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Add the record on the primary/writable DNS server (or convert zone to AD-integrated when appropriate)
Disable recursion on the DNS server
Add 8.8.8.8 as a forwarder and retry
Turn off secure dynamic updates
